impact: The local-first sync engine advances the observation/growth cursors (pullSince/pushSince) to the server's highWater = new Date().toISOString() (wall-clock), while log entries carry their own (possibly earlier) timestamps and the server filters with `timestamp > since`. This creates a narrow data-loss window for the two cursor-gated append logs (observations, growth): under client/server clock skew (server clock leads on push) or a back-dated entry becoming visible after another machine's pull stamped highWater, an entry whose timestamp ends up <= an already-advanced cursor can be permanently skipped — dedup never recovers it because the cursor gates what the server SENDS. Acceptable for v1 single-user (sync at session boundaries, rarely concurrent; spec states correctness rests on dedup keys, not cursor precision; sessions use forgiving day-granularity resend; reinforcements/lessons are sent in full so have no window). Follow-up: advance the observation/growth cursor to max(entry timestamp actually seen) rather than server wall-clock now(), which closes the clock-skew skip entirely. Surfaced by the T-043 final holistic review.
resolution: Closed the clock-skew skip window in src/sync.ts. Added an advanceCursor(current, entries) helper that moves the observation/growth cursor (pullSince/pushSince) to max(current, latest entry timestamp actually processed) instead of the server's wall-clock highWater. pull() now advances pullSince over [...observations, ...growth] received; push() advances pushSince over [...observations, ...growth] sent; the server-returned highWater is intentionally ignored for the cursor (a 2xx confirms acceptance). Comparison is numeric (Date.getTime) to stay robust to ISO formatting differences and consistent with the server's `new Date(timestamp).getTime() > since` filter, and the cursor never regresses. This guarantees any entry the server has not yet surfaced has timestamp >= the cursor and remains eligible next exchange, so skew or a back-dated entry can no longer permanently skip it. Updated two existing assertions that encoded the old highWater behavior and added 3 regression tests (empty pull does not advance; cursor takes max of obs+growth; empty push does not advance). Verified: typecheck clean, 179/179 tests pass.
title: Sync cursor uses server wall-clock highWater; advance to max entry timestamp to close clock-skew skip window
